activity.title: I am excited to share that this past May, I graduated from Quinnipiac University . During my time at Quinnipiac, I had the opportunity to pursue majors in Economics, Mathematics, and Data Science while working alongside faculty and fellow students who challenged me to think rigorously and pursue research I genuinely enjoyed. These experiences sparked my interest in quantitative macroeconomics, econometrics, and dynamic economic modeling. I am incredibly grateful to Donn Johnson , Christopher Ball , Jesse Kalinowski, Aman Desai , Jill Shahverdian , and all of the mentors, friends, and family who supported me throughout my undergraduate journey. I am also excited to share that this fall I will be joining the University of Rochester as a Ph.D. student in Economics, continuing to develop my research interests while contributing to the department's research community. Thank you to everyone who has been part of this journey, and I look forward to what lies ahead.

we won the headline track at Caltech 's premier hackathon Hacktech ! we built Sentinel — a physical-security architect. scan a room with LiDAR, watch the space reconstruct as a 3D point cloud, and K2 Think V2 reasons through where every camera should go: FOV coverage, sight-line obstruction, entry-point prioritization, budget tradeoffs. drag a slider from $500 to $25k and the placement re-optimizes live. LLMs alone can't do 3D coverage reasoning. ask one to place 4 cameras to cover 95% of a floor and you get hallucinated coordinates. so we externalized the geometry via point cloud + raycasting and let K2 reason semantically on top. spatial substrate + adversarial reasoning + a UI that lets you walk through your future system. huge shoutout to my cracked team Alex Li , Rahul Palani , and Suhaan Khurana for your trust and hard work. had the most fun shipping with you guys! can't wait to spam CUAs on our Mac minis 😎 live site: http://oppcam.tech/ demo: https://lnkd.in/gfb-g_iZ github: https://lnkd.in/gaxR7bct devpost: https://lnkd.in/gJ5wErsE

We won at Hacktech 2026 hosted by Caltech this past weekend! Building sentinel this past weekend with Melody Yang , Suhaan Khurana , and Rahul Palani was such a fun experience. We won first overall for best use of AI and each took home Mac Minis. Burglary losses alone account for more than $3B annually. Studies have shown that installing proper security cameras can lead to a 50% reduction in theft. So, we built Sentinel, an AI-powered system that 1. Analyzes building layouts from a simple phone recording 2. Determines optimal security camera placements 3. Maximizes coverage using spatial reasoning and simulation A wholehearted thank you to all the HackTech organizers, sponsors, and judges for such a well run hackathon (and the free boba).
